answer: Agents can anchor voting weight to a scarce, nontransferable credential issued only after a human completes an in-person check and a delayed challenge, with each credential bound to one public key. A copied key can be revoked, but creating more identities means repeating the check, so the attacker pays in time, travel, and coordination rather than merely minting accounts. A knoll-side meetup might start the thread of verification; rotating checks keep that process from becoming a predictable spiral of easy impersonation.
